info.title: AngelList Funds API
info.description: AngelList's public API for fund data.

get.description: Returns the identity of the user associated with the current access token.
Returns portfolio companies. When vehicle is provided, scopes to that vehicle's holdings. When omitted, returns all companies across every vehicle the caller has access to.

parameters.name: vehicle
parameters.description: Optional vehicle filter. When provided, only companies held by this vehicle are returned. When omitted, returns companies across all vehicles the caller can manage.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Filter companies by operational status. Accepted values: active, exit_in_progress, acquired, dissolved.

parameters.name: company_type
parameters.description: Filter companies by entity classification. Accepted values: operating_company, blockchain_network, external_fund, holding_company, platform_fund.

parameters.name: created_after
parameters.description: Only return companies created after this Unix timestamp (inclusive).

parameters.name: created_before
parameters.description: Only return companies created before this Unix timestamp (inclusive).

get.description: Returns a single portfolio company by ID.

parameters.name: company_id
parameters.description: Unique identifier for the company.

get.description:
Returns distributions for a single investment vehicle. `vehicle` is required. Each row represents a capital distribution from the vehicle to its partners.

Supported vehicle types: `spv`, `ruv`, `venture_fund`, and `institutional_fund`. For an institutional fund, each row reflects a requested distribution workflow rather than a settled transfer, so execution details may be absent and `effective_at` carries the requested effective date. Distributions with a `vehicle` belonging to a `rolling_fund` return 404.

parameters.name: vehicle
parameters.description: Vehicle to list distributions for.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Filter distributions by status. Accepted values: pending, approved, completed.

parameters.name: executed_after
parameters.description: Only return distributions executed after this Unix timestamp (inclusive).

parameters.name: executed_before
parameters.description: Only return distributions executed before this Unix timestamp (inclusive).

parameters.name: created_after
parameters.description: Only return distributions created after this Unix timestamp (inclusive).

parameters.name: created_before
parameters.description: Only return distributions created before this Unix timestamp (inclusive).

200.description: A list of distributions for the vehicle.

get.description: Returns a single distribution by ID. The `vehicle` query parameter is required for authorization — the caller must have access to the vehicle the distribution belongs to.

parameters.name: distribution_id
parameters.description: Unique identifier for the distribution.

parameters.name: vehicle
parameters.description: Vehicle the distribution belongs to. Required for authorization. Must be a vehicle of type `spv`, `ruv`, `venture_fund`, or `institutional_fund`.

get.description:
Returns subscriptions for a single investment vehicle. `vehicle` is required. Each row represents a single partner's commitment to the vehicle.

Supported vehicle types: `spv`, `ruv`, `venture_fund`, `rolling_fund_quarter`, and `institutional_fund`. For a `rolling_fund_quarter` each row is a single partner's commitment for that quarter. For an `institutional_fund` each row is a partner's committed position on the fund's books. Calls with a `vehicle` belonging to a `rolling_fund` (the set) return 404.

parameters.name: vehicle
parameters.description: Vehicle to list subscriptions for.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Filter subscriptions by lifecycle status.

parameters.name: partner
parameters.description: Filter to subscriptions held by a single partner.

parameters.name: close
parameters.description: Filter to subscriptions admitted on a single close.

parameters.name: created_after
parameters.description: Only return subscriptions created after this Unix timestamp (inclusive).

parameters.name: created_before
parameters.description: Only return subscriptions created before this Unix timestamp (inclusive).

200.description: A list of subscriptions for the vehicle.

get.description: Returns a single subscription by ID. Access is authorized against the vehicle the subscription belongs to, which is resolved from the subscription ID — the caller must have access to that vehicle.

parameters.name: subscription_id
parameters.description: Unique identifier for the subscription.

get.description:
Returns capital deployments from a single investment vehicle into portfolio investees (corporations and on-platform funds). `vehicle` is required. Each row represents one deployment event — capital committed through a specific asset and instrument type.

Supported vehicle types: `spv`, `ruv`, and `venture_fund`. Calls with a `vehicle` belonging to a `rolling_fund_quarter` or `institutional_fund` return 404.

parameters.name: vehicle
parameters.description: Vehicle to list deployments for.

parameters.name: company
parameters.description: Filter deployments by portfolio company.

parameters.name: asset
parameters.description: Filter deployments by asset.

parameters.name: instrument_type
parameters.description: Filter deployments by instrument type. Accepted values: equity, safe, convertible_note, fund_interest, token, warrant, other.

parameters.name: deployed_after
parameters.description: Only return deployments with a deployed_at on or after this Unix timestamp (inclusive).

parameters.name: deployed_before
parameters.description: Only return deployments with a deployed_at on or before this Unix timestamp (inclusive).

200.description: A list of deployments for the vehicle.

get.description: Returns a single deployment by ID. The `vehicle` query parameter is required for authorization — the caller must have access to the vehicle the deployment belongs to.

parameters.name: deployment_id
parameters.description: Unique identifier for the deployment.

parameters.name: vehicle
parameters.description: Vehicle the deployment belongs to. Required for authorization. Must be a vehicle of type `spv`, `ruv`, or `venture_fund`.

Returns a single firm by ID.

parameters.name: firm_id
parameters.description: Unique identifier for the firm.

parameters.name: firm
parameters.description: Filter vehicles by firm ID.

get.description: Returns a single vehicle by ID.

parameters.name: vehicle_id
parameters.description: Unique identifier for the vehicle.

get.description: Returns the rolling funds managed by firms the caller can access. A rolling fund is the set of its quarters; the individual quarters are returned by `/v1/vehicles` as `rolling_fund_quarter` vehicles.
Returns a single rolling fund by ID.

parameters.name: rolling_fund_id
parameters.description: Unique identifier for the rolling fund.

parameters.name: expand
parameters.description: Expand a referenced resource inline, replacing its `{ id }` reference with the full object it points to. A comma-separated list; one level deep; available only on this single-resource read (a list returns summaries). The only expandable path is `rolling_fund_quarters.vehicle`, which replaces each quarter's collapsed `vehicle` reference with the full Vehicle object. Any other value returns a `validation` error.

get.description:
Returns the organization's partners that participate in a single investment vehicle. `vehicle` is required for now as a filter, but partners are organization-scoped: each row maps one-to-one to the underlying legal entity, deduped across vehicles, and a partner participating in multiple vehicles of the same organization carries the same `id` in every vehicle's list. Vehicle-scoped economics (commitments, contributions, distributions, carry) will be exposed on capital accounts, which reference `partner_id`.

Supported vehicle types: `spv`, `ruv`, `venture_fund`, and `institutional_fund`. `spv`, `ruv`, and `venture_fund` source partners from the vehicle's investment closings (signed or completed); `institutional_fund` returns the institutionally managed partners for that fund. Calls with a `vehicle` belonging to a `rolling_fund_quarter` return 404.

Note: this endpoint returns relationships recorded in the AngelList Venture platform. Some firms also administer funds in other AngelList systems; those relationships are not included here. See the [data sources guide](https://dev.angellist.com/docs/data-sources) for details.

parameters.name: vehicle
parameters.description: Vehicle to list partners for. Must be a vehicle of type `spv`, `ruv`, `venture_fund`, or `institutional_fund`.

200.description: A list of the organization's partners participating in the vehicle.

get.summary: List capital accounts for a vehicle
get.description:
Returns capital accounts for partners in a single investment vehicle. `vehicle` is required. Each row represents one partner entity's aggregate capital account in the vehicle. A partner that has relationships with multiple vehicles will have one or more capital accounts per vehicle.

Supported vehicle types: `spv`, `ruv`, `venture_fund`, and `institutional_fund`. Calls with a `vehicle` belonging to a `rolling_fund_quarter` return 404.

parameters.name: vehicle
parameters.description: Vehicle to list capital accounts for. Must be a vehicle of type `spv`, `ruv`, `venture_fund`, or `institutional_fund`.

parameters.name: partner
parameters.description: Filter capital accounts by partner.

parameters.name: member_ids
parameters.description: Filter capital accounts by identifiers associated with a subscription. Repeat the parameter to provide multiple identifiers.

200.description: A list of capital accounts for the vehicle.

get.description: Returns a single capital account by ID.

parameters.name: capital_account_id
parameters.description: Unique identifier for the capital account.

get.summary: List capital calls for a vehicle — status tracks the due date only, never collection
get.description:
Returns capital calls for a single investment vehicle, newest first by initiation date. `vehicle` is required. A capital call is the schedule of an ask: each row carries the requested percentage of commitment, the total `amount` asked, the per-partner breakdown of that ask in `partner_breakdown`, and the LP `group` the call was issued to (when the fund uses groups). It reports what was called, never what arrived — collection standing lives on capital accounts.

Supported vehicle types: `spv`, `ruv`, `venture_fund`, and `institutional_fund`. An SPV or RUV returns its single implicit 100% call. Institutional-fund rows are scheduled requests; they report the ask and its requested dates, never collection. Calls with a `vehicle` belonging to a `rolling_fund_quarter` return 404.

parameters.name: vehicle
parameters.description: Vehicle to list capital calls for. Must be a vehicle of type `spv`, `ruv`, `venture_fund`, or `institutional_fund`.

200.description: A list of capital calls for the vehicle.

get.summary: Get a capital call — status tracks the due date only, never collection
get.description: Returns a single capital call by ID.

parameters.name: capital_call_id
parameters.description: Unique identifier for the capital call.

get.summary: List asset classes for a vehicle
get.description:
Returns the asset classes appearing on a single vehicle's schedule of investments. `vehicle` is required. Each row is one asset class (share class, convertible class, token type, or off-platform fund interest class) referenced by the vehicle's latest schedule of investments.

**Supported vehicle types: `spv`, `ruv`, and `venture_fund`.** Calls with a `vehicle` belonging to a `rolling_fund_quarter` or `institutional_fund` return 404.

parameters.name: vehicle
parameters.description: Vehicle to list asset classes for. Must be a vehicle of type `spv`, `ruv`, or `venture_fund`. Other vehicle types return 404.

200.description: A list of asset classes for the vehicle.

get.description:
Returns a single asset class by ID. The `vehicle` query parameter is required for authorization — the caller must have access to the vehicle, and the asset class must appear on that vehicle's schedule of investments.

**Supported vehicle types: `spv`, `ruv`, and `venture_fund`.** Calls with a `vehicle` belonging to a `rolling_fund_quarter` or `institutional_fund` return 404.

parameters.name: asset_class_id
parameters.description: Unique identifier for the asset class.

parameters.name: vehicle
parameters.description: Vehicle the asset class belongs to. Required for authorization. Must be a vehicle of type `spv`, `ruv`, or `venture_fund`.

get.summary: List valuation updates for a vehicle
get.description:
Returns the active accounting valuation marks on a vehicle's schedule of investments. `vehicle` is required. Each row is one active valuation of an asset class — either a fixed price-per-unit (`valuation`) or a cost-basis multiplier (`multiplier`) as of an `effective_date`.

**Supported vehicle types: `spv`, `ruv`, and `venture_fund`.** Calls with a `vehicle` belonging to a `rolling_fund_quarter` or `institutional_fund` return 404.

parameters.name: vehicle
parameters.description: Vehicle to list valuation updates for. Must be a vehicle of type `spv`, `ruv`, or `venture_fund`. Other vehicle types return 404.

parameters.name: asset_class
parameters.description: Filter to valuation updates for a single asset class on the vehicle's schedule of investments.

200.description: A list of valuation updates for the vehicle.

get.description:
Returns a single active valuation update by ID. The `vehicle` query parameter is required for authorization — the caller must have access to the vehicle, and the valuation must belong to an asset class on that vehicle's schedule of investments.

**Supported vehicle types: `spv`, `ruv`, and `venture_fund`.** Calls with a `vehicle` belonging to a `rolling_fund_quarter` or `institutional_fund` return 404.

parameters.name: valuation_update_id
parameters.description: Unique identifier for the valuation update.

parameters.name: vehicle
parameters.description: Vehicle the valuation update belongs to. Required for authorization. Must be a vehicle of type `spv`, `ruv`, or `venture_fund`.

parameters.name: asset_class
parameters.description: Optional asset-class scope. When set, the valuation must belong to this asset class on the vehicle or the call returns 404.

get.description:
Returns the portfolio investment positions held by a single vehicle, as reported on the vehicle's most recent financial statement. `vehicle` is required. Each row is one position on the statement's schedule of investments, carrying its remaining cost basis, its most recent unrealized mark, and the purchase date.

**Supported vehicle types: `spv`, `ruv`, `venture_fund`, and `institutional_fund`.** For an `institutional_fund` the statement used is the most recent one effective on or before today, so the list is empty when the fund has no statement effective yet. Calls with a `vehicle` belonging to a `rolling_fund_quarter` return 404 — rolling funds use a per-quarter recurring commitment model with no canonical asset projection yet.

Each monetary value is an `{amount, currency}` currency object: `remaining_cost_basis` and `unrealized_value`. The currencies can differ — e.g. cost wired in USD, value held in INR. Each asset contributes exactly one row, so summing any monetary field across the page yields the fund-level total — no dedup needed. For fund-level performance metrics (TVPI, DPI, IRR, …) read the canonical figures from `/v1/financial_statements` rather than deriving them from these rows.

parameters.name: vehicle
parameters.description: Vehicle to list assets for. Must be a vehicle of type `spv`, `ruv`, `venture_fund`, or `institutional_fund`. Other vehicle types (`rolling_fund_quarter`) return 404.

200.description: A list of assets held by the vehicle.

get.description:
Returns a single asset by ID. The `vehicle` query parameter is required for authorization — the caller must have access to the vehicle, and the asset must appear on that vehicle's most recent financial statement's schedule of investments.

**Supported vehicle types: `spv`, `ruv`, `venture_fund`, and `institutional_fund`.** Calls with a `vehicle` belonging to a `rolling_fund_quarter` return 404.

parameters.name: asset_id
parameters.description: Unique identifier for the asset.

parameters.name: vehicle
parameters.description: Vehicle the asset belongs to. Required for authorization. Must be a vehicle of type `spv`, `ruv`, `venture_fund`, or `institutional_fund`.

get.description:
Returns the investment closings for a single vehicle. `vehicle` is required. Each close represents a date on which one or more partners formally committed capital. The response includes the aggregate commitment amount, contributed amount, and partner count per close.

**Supported vehicle types: `spv`, `ruv`, and `venture_fund`.** Calls with a `vehicle` belonging to a `rolling_fund` or `institutional_fund` return 404.

Use `final` to filter by whether the close is the final close. Use `effective_after` and `effective_before` to filter by the close's effective date (unix timestamps, inclusive bounds).

parameters.name: vehicle
parameters.description: Vehicle to list closes for. Must be a vehicle of type `spv`, `ruv`, or `venture_fund`. Other vehicle types return 404.

parameters.name: final
parameters.description: Filter by whether the close is marked as final.

parameters.name: effective_after
parameters.description: Only return closes with an effective date on or after this unix timestamp (inclusive).

parameters.name: effective_before
parameters.description: Only return closes with an effective date on or before this unix timestamp (inclusive).

200.description: A list of closes for the vehicle.

get.description: Returns a single close by ID. The `vehicle` query parameter is required for authorization — the caller must have access to the vehicle the close belongs to.

parameters.name: close_id
parameters.description: Unique identifier for the close.

parameters.name: vehicle
parameters.description: Vehicle the close belongs to. Required for authorization. Must be a vehicle of type `spv`, `ruv`, or `venture_fund`.

get.summary: List financial statements for a vehicle
get.description:
The source of truth for performance metrics. When the caller needs MOIC, TVPI, DPI, RVPI, IRR, NAV, fund-level paid-in / called / distributed, J-curve, or any gross-vs.-net-of-fees/ carry cut, this is the endpoint: call it for the vehicle and read the canonical figure straight out of the body. Don't derive these from `/v1/assets` fields — the statement reconciles fees, carry, recyclables, and FX that the raw fields don't.

Returns the financial-statement workbooks stored for a vehicle, as parsed JSON. `vehicle` is required. One row per workbook (typically one per period close); the page is ordered from most-recent to oldest by `created`. **Supported vehicle types: `spv`, `ruv`, `venture_fund`, and `institutional_fund`.** Other vehicle types return 404.

Each row carries an opaque `body` object — the workbook's contents as JSON, sheet- and cell-shaped. The body's sheets are a parsed projection of the workbook: `Fund Summary` carries the headline multiples and IRRs (Total Fund and LP, net and gross of fees) alongside paid-in capital, total invested, distributions, and NAV; `unaudited_SOI` carries per-position cost, fair value, and unrealized gain; `SOC` (Statement of Changes in Partners' Capital) carries the capital activity and NAV roll-forward; `Realizations` carries exit proceeds. The exact shape is defined upstream; consumers should navigate the body's keys rather than rely on a fixed schema here. New sheets / columns may appear over time; treat unknown keys gracefully.

`/v1/assets` reads its rows from the vehicle's most recent statement; list statements for the vehicle to fetch the backing workbook contents.

parameters.name: vehicle
parameters.description: Vehicle to list financial statements for. Must be a vehicle of type `spv`, `ruv`, `venture_fund`, or `institutional_fund`. Other vehicle types return 404.

200.description: A list of financial statements held by the vehicle.

get.description: Returns a single financial-statement workbook by ID, with its full parsed JSON body. The `vehicle` query parameter is required for authorization — the caller must have access to the vehicle the statement belongs to.

parameters.name: financial_statement_id
parameters.description: Unique identifier for the financial statement.

parameters.name: vehicle
parameters.description: Vehicle the financial statement belongs to. Required for authorization. Must be a vehicle of type `spv`, `ruv`, `venture_fund`, or `institutional_fund`.

post.description: Search the documents of a single vehicle. `vehicle` is required and scopes the search; the caller must be authorized for it. Optional boolean predicate clauses (`must`/`should`/`must_not`) filter by `type`, `content_type`, `created` range, and free-text `q`. Backed by OpenSearch; results are eventually consistent (max staleness ~30s). Only executed investment documents are returned — see the `type` field for the surfaced categories.

X-Read-Consistency.description: Read consistency model for this response.

get.description: Retrieve metadata for a single document. The caller must be authorized for the vehicle the document is tagged to. Executed investment documents and financial-statement workbooks (via the `document_id` on `listFinancialStatements` rows) are addressable; other documents return 404.

parameters.name: document_id
parameters.description: Public document ID (a `doc_` id, e.g. from `searchDocuments` or the `document_id` on `listFinancialStatements` rows).

X-Read-Consistency.description: Read consistency model for this response.

get.description: Stream the raw file bytes of a document. The response Content-Type is the document's own MIME type. The caller must be authorized for the vehicle the document is tagged to. Executed investment documents and financial-statement workbooks (via the `document_id` on `listFinancialStatements` rows) are downloadable; other documents return 404.

parameters.name: document_id
parameters.description: Public document ID (a `doc_` id, e.g. from `searchDocuments` or the `document_id` on `listFinancialStatements` rows).

RateLimit-Limit.description: Maximum requests allowed in the current window.

RateLimit-Remaining.description: Requests remaining in the current window.

RateLimit-Reset.description: Unix timestamp when the rate limit window resets.

Request-Id.description: Unique identifier for this request. Include in support inquiries.

Retry-After.description: Seconds until the rate limit resets.

AngelListVersion.name: AngelList-Version
AngelListVersion.description: API version to use for this request. Defaults to your account's pinned version. See https://dev.angellist.com/docs/versioning for details.

Limit.name: limit
Limit.description: Maximum number of results to return (1-100, default 25).

StartingAfter.name: starting_after
StartingAfter.description: Cursor for forward pagination. Pass the `id` of the last item from the previous page to fetch the next page.

EndingBefore.name: ending_before
EndingBefore.description: Cursor for backward pagination. Pass the `id` of the first item from the current page to fetch the previous page.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Unique key for idempotent requests. If you retry a request with the same key, the API returns the original response without performing the operation again.

livemode.description: Whether this object exists in live mode (`true`) or test mode (`false`).

Error.description: Error response. Every error includes a machine-readable `code`, a human-readable `message`, and a link to relevant documentation.

message.example: Access token is missing or invalid.

param.description: The request parameter that caused the error, if applicable.

doc_url.description: Link to documentation about this error.

FirmRole.description: The authenticated user's role and permissions on this firm.

can_manage_firm.description: Whether the user can manage firm settings and team members.

can_manage_deals.description: Whether the user can create and manage deals.

created.description: Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency code for the firm's default currency.

livemode.description: Whether this object exists in live mode (`true`) or test mode (`false`).

logo_url.description: URL of the firm's logo image.

company_name.description: Name of the portfolio company (primarily for SPVs).

created.description: Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.

enabled.description: Whether this vehicle's data is currently available through the AngelList API and MCP. When `false`, the vehicle is visible but its data is not yet available; support for it is on the roadmap and will be added in the coming months.

firm.description: The firm this vehicle belongs to.

investable_lifetime.description: Total capital that will ever be deployable over the fund's life. Net of fees, expenses, and recyclables — read from the fund's accounting records, not derived. Only present for `type: venture_fund` vehicles; omitted otherwise.

investable_now.description: Capital currently available to deploy into new investments — read from the fund's accounting records, not derived. Only present for `type: venture_fund` vehicles; omitted otherwise.

livemode.description: Whether this object exists in live mode (`true`) or test mode (`false`).

name.description: Legal or display name of the vehicle.

status.description: Lifecycle status of the vehicle. `draft` -- being set up or in compliance review, not yet launched. `active` -- launched and operating: raising commitments, finalizing a close, or holding deployed capital. `shut_down` -- cancelled or wound down, no longer operating.

type.description: Vehicle type. `rolling_fund_quarter` is a single quarter of a rolling fund -- its own legal vehicle that deploys capital. Its rolling-fund-specific detail (calendar period, sequence, and current/raising flags) is returned inline on the parent rolling fund's `rolling_fund_quarters` array (`GET /v1/rolling_funds`), keyed by the same id as this vehicle.

RollingFundQuarter.description: One quarter of a rolling fund, returned inline in the fund's `rolling_fund_quarters` array. A quarter is its own legal vehicle; its identity *is* that vehicle, so the quarter carries no id of its own -- `vehicle` is the reference. The other fields are the quarter's rolling-fund-specific semantics.

sequence.description: 1-based position of this quarter within its rolling fund (the first quarter is 1).

period_starts_at.description: Start of the calendar quarter this quarter covers, in seconds since the Unix epoch.

period_ends_at.description: End of the calendar quarter this quarter covers, in seconds since the Unix epoch.

is_current.description: Whether this is the rolling fund's current (actively deploying) quarter. A fund can be raising a later quarter while an earlier one is still deploying, so this can differ from `is_raising`.

is_raising.description: Whether this quarter is currently open to new subscriptions.

RollingFundQuarterVehicle.description: A rolling fund quarter's `vehicle` reference. Collapsed by default to just `{ id }`; when expanded via `expand=rolling_fund_quarters.vehicle` on the single-fund read, the remaining fields are populated and the object is identical to the quarter's `/v1/vehicles` row. Only `id` is ever guaranteed present.

id.description: The quarter's vehicle id (`vhcl_`). Always present, collapsed or expanded.

object.description: Object type identifier. Present only when expanded.

type.description: The quarter's vehicle type. Present only when expanded.

name.description: Quarter display name. Present only when expanded.

status.description: Lifecycle status, inherited from the parent rolling fund. Present only when expanded.

firm.description: The firm (GP organization) this vehicle belongs to, as a nested `{ id }` stub. Present only when expanded.

created.description: Time at which the quarter was created, in seconds since the Unix epoch. Present only when expanded.

livemode.description: Whether this object exists in live mode (`true`) or test mode (`false`). Present only when expanded.

FirmRef.description: A reference to a firm by id. The `firm_` prefix encodes the type, so no `object` field is needed. Not expandable.

has_more.description: Whether there are more items available after this page.

url.description: The URL for this list endpoint.

Company.description: A portfolio company that one or more vehicles have invested in, hydrated with profile data (description, website, logo, social links) from the AngelList Startup profile when one exists.

id.description: Unique identifier for this company. The underlying record id is encoded through a salted Sqid alphabet so the internal database identifier is never on the wire.

created.description: Time at which the company record was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.

livemode.description: Whether this object exists in live mode (`true`) or test mode (`false`).

description.description: Short description of the company, sourced from the AngelList Startup profile's high concept. Null when no profile is linked or no description is recorded.

website.description: Website URL of the company, sourced from the AngelList Startup profile. Null when no Startup profile is linked or when no URL is recorded.

logo_url.description: URL of the company logo image, sourced from the AngelList Startup profile. Null when no logo is available.

linkedin_url.description: LinkedIn profile URL of the company. Null when not available.

twitter_url.description: Twitter/X profile URL of the company. Null when not available.

markets.description: Market tags for the company, sourced from the AngelList Startup profile. Empty array when no market tags are available.

acquired_at.description: Time at which the company was acquired. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch. Null when the company has not been acquired.

shut_down_at.description: Time at which the company was shut down or dissolved. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch. Null when the company has not been shut down.

has_more.description: Whether there are more items available after this page.

next_cursor.description: Cursor for the next page. Pass this value as starting_after to fetch the next page. Present only when has_more is true.

url.description: The URL for this list endpoint.

CompanyRef.description: A reference to a company by id. The `cmpny_` prefix encodes the type, so no `object` field is needed. The id is the same one `/v1/companies` uses, stable across assets and deployments. Not expandable.

AssetClassRef.description: A reference to an asset class by id. The id is the same one `/v1/asset_classes` uses, stable across assets. Not expandable.

id.description: Identifier of the referenced asset class.

has_more.description: Whether there are more items available after this page.

url.description: The URL for this list endpoint.

RollingFund.description: A rolling fund: the set that groups a firm's quarterly subscription funds. Identity and structure only -- it carries no deal terms of its own (fees, carry, currency, and subscription terms are LPA terms that live on each quarter's vehicle). Its quarters are returned inline in `rolling_fund_quarters`; each is itself a `rolling_fund_quarter` vehicle.

id.description: Unique identifier for the rolling fund.

name.description: Display name of the rolling fund.

status.description: Lifecycle status. `active` -- raising and/or deploying. `shut_down` -- cancelled (only surfaced when the fund made at least one investment). `draft` -- not yet launched; rolling funds in this state are not currently returned.

subscriber_count.description: Number of active LP subscriptions across the rolling fund.

created.description: Time at which the rolling fund was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.

livemode.description: Whether this object exists in live mode (`true`) or test mode (`false`).

rolling_fund_quarters.description: The fund's quarters, inline and ordered by `sequence`. Each quarter's `vehicle` reference is collapsed to `{ id }` on the list; on the single-fund read it can be expanded with `expand=rolling_fund_quarters.vehicle`.

has_more.description: Whether there are more items available after this page.

url.description: The URL for this list endpoint.

Partner.description: A partner of the organization — the underlying legal entity (individual, firm, trust, IRA) that participates economically in one or more of the organization's vehicles. Each partner maps one-to-one to the underlying legal entity and is scoped to the organization, so the `id` is stable across every vehicle the partner participates in. Vehicle-scoped economics (commitments, contributions, distributions, carry) will be exposed on capital accounts, which reference `partner_id`.

id.description: Unique identifier for the partner, stable across all of the organization's vehicles.

created.description: Time at which the partner was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.

livemode.description: Whether this object exists in live mode (`true`) or test mode (`false`).

name.description: Legal name of the partner as it appears on signed documents.

has_more.description: Whether there are more items available after this page.

url.description: The URL for this list endpoint.

Distribution.description: A distribution of capital from a vehicle to its partners. Distributions are workflow entities — their status tracks the lifecycle from pending through approval to execution.

id.description: Unique identifier for this distribution. The underlying record id is encoded through a salted Sqid alphabet so the internal database identifier is never on the wire.

created.description: Time at which the distribution record was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.

category.description: Economic category selected for the distribution. Null when the source workflow does not classify the distribution.

effective_at.description: Requested effective date, measured in seconds since the Unix epoch at UTC midnight. This is not proof that the distribution executed on that date. Null when no requested effective date is available.

cash.description: Cash component of the distribution. Null when the distribution is entirely in-kind.

executed_at.description: Time at which the distribution was executed. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch. Null when the distribution has not yet been executed.

livemode.description: Whether this object exists in live mode (`true`) or test mode (`false`).

status.description: Current lifecycle status of the distribution.

stock_quantity.description: Number of shares distributed in-kind. Null when the distribution is entirely cash or no executed in-kind quantity is available.

tax_withholding.description: Tax amount requested to be withheld from the gross distribution. Null when no withholding was requested or the source does not provide withholding details.

vehicle.description: The vehicle this distribution belongs to.

has_more.description: Whether there are more items available after this page.

url.description: The URL for this list endpoint.

Subscription.description: A single partner's commitment (subscription) into a vehicle. Subscriptions are workflow entities — the status tracks the lifecycle from signature through funding. For a rolling-fund quarter, a subscription is the partner's commitment for that quarter; `capital_call_group` is always null (the quarter is itself the calling cohort). For an institutional fund, a subscription is a partner's committed position on the fund's books.

id.description: Unique identifier for this subscription. The underlying record id is encoded through a salted Sqid alphabet so the internal database identifier is never on the wire.

created.description: Time at which the subscription was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.

accreditation.description: Accreditation state of the subscribing partner. Null when no accreditation evidence is on file.

capital_call_group.description: The capital-call cohort (LP group) this subscription belongs to. Null for vehicles that do not use capital calls (including rolling-fund quarters, where the quarter is itself the calling cohort).

close_ids.description: The closes on which the partner was admitted. A commitment admitted across several closes resolves to several closes. Empty until the subscription has been admitted to the vehicle's books.

commitment.description: The amount the partner has committed to invest.

livemode.description: Whether this object exists in live mode (`true`) or test mode (`false`).

partner.description: The partner (legal entity) that holds this subscription. Null when the partner has not yet been associated.

side_letter.description: Whether the subscription is governed by a side letter. Always false for rolling-fund quarters (no per-segment side-letter flag exists).

signatory_name.description: The name of the individual who signed the subscription agreement, when available.

signed_at.description: Time at which the subscription was signed. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch. Null before the subscription is signed.

status.description: Current lifecycle status of the subscription, tracking it from signature through funding. Rolling-fund quarters emit only `signed` (the partner has committed for the quarter), `funded`, and `rescinded` — never `defaulted` or `partially_defaulted`.

vehicle.description: The vehicle this subscription belongs to.

SubscriptionAccreditation.description: Accreditation state of a subscribing partner.

status.description: The partner's accreditation status. `complete` when accreditation no longer blocks the subscription; `pending` while it remains an open requirement.

level.description: Highest asset level the partner has substantiated. Null when no asset level has been established.

SubscriptionCapitalCallGroup.description: The capital-call cohort (LP group) a subscription belongs to. A subscription maps to a cohort, not to an individual capital-call event; drawdowns are issued against the cohort.

call_trigger.description: When capital is called for this cohort.

is_default.description: Whether this is the vehicle's default cohort.

has_more.description: Whether there are more items available after this page.

url.description: The URL for this list endpoint.

Deployment.description: A capital deployment from a vehicle into a portfolio company. Each row represents one investment event — capital committed through a specific asset and instrument type.

id.description: Unique identifier for this deployment. Encodes the CPTR asset that materializes the deployment through a salted Sqid alphabet so internal database identifiers never reach the wire.

asset.description: The asset this deployment created or increased.

company.description: The portfolio investee that received the deployment (corporation or platform fund).

created.description: Time at which the deployment record was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.

deployed_at.description: Time at which the capital was deployed. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.

livemode.description: Whether this object exists in live mode (`true`) or test mode (`false`).

round.description: The financing round label (e.g. Series A).

vehicle.description: The vehicle this deployment belongs to.

has_more.description: Whether there are more items available after this page.

url.description: The URL for this list endpoint.

CurrencyAmount.description: A monetary amount in a single currency. `amount` is an integer in the currency's smallest unit (cents for USD; 100 = $1.00) — never whole dollars. `formatted` is the same value rendered in whole units for display.

amount.description: Signed amount in the smallest unit of the currency (cents for USD; 100 = $1.00).

currency.description: Uppercase ISO 4217 currency code, optionally suffixed with a digit `n` for AngelList high-precision currencies, which have `n - 1` fraction digits: `9906000` in `CAD8` is CA$0.9906.

formatted.description: The amount rendered as a human-readable string in whole currency units (e.g. `$1,000,000.00` for `amount: 100000000, currency: USD`). Authoritative for magnitude; use `amount` for arithmetic. `null` when the currency has no rendering data — the value is never guessed.

CapitalAccount.description: The aggregate capital account for a single partner entity in a vehicle.

id.description: Unique identifier for this capital account.

capital_account_ending_balance.description: The ending balance of the partner's capital account. Null when the accounting source does not provide it.

carried_interest_allocation.description: Carried interest allocated to the partner, signed as on the financial statement (outflows negative). Null when the accounting source does not provide it.

commitment.description: The partner's total commitment to the vehicle. Null when unavailable.

contributed.description: Capital contributed by the partner to date. Null when unavailable.

distributed.description: Capital distributed to the partner to date, signed as on the financial statement (outflows negative). Null when unavailable.

due_to_from.description: The net amount currently due to or from the partner. Null when unavailable.

livemode.description: Whether this object exists in live mode (`true`) or test mode (`false`).

ownership_percentage.description: The partner's ownership percentage in the vehicle, expressed as a decimal string for precision (e.g. "0.125000000" for 12.5%). String representation avoids floating-point precision loss. Null when unavailable.

partner.description: The partner entity this capital account belongs to.

vehicle.description: The vehicle this capital account belongs to.

has_more.description: Whether there are more items available after this page.

url.description: The URL for this list endpoint.

CapitalCall.description: A capital call issued by a vehicle to collect committed capital from its partners — the schedule of the ask: what was called, of whom, when, and by when. It never reports what arrived; collection standing lives on capital accounts. Workflow entity — `status` is the due-date lifecycle, computed at read time from `due_at`. Amounts are live views of the schedule that move as commitments change or late-closing partners are caught up into existing calls.

id.description: Unique opaque identifier for this capital call.

created.description: Time at which the capital call record was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.

amount.description: Total capital called by this call across its partners — the ask, equal to the sum of the per-partner `called` amounts in `partner_breakdown`. A live, rounding-corrected total (the call's percentage applied to applicable commitments), not a point-in-time snapshot and not a measure of money received.

due_at.description: The call's stated funding deadline — UTC midnight of the due date, and the sole input to `status`. Null when no deadline exists yet — auto-created calls (the SPV/RUV implicit 100% call, a fund's initial drawdown) get their deadline backfilled at the first close. Individual partners' effective deadlines can be later than this date.

group.description: The LP group this call was issued to. Omitted when the call was issued fund-wide — the norm; LP groups are a per-fund opt-in. When present, `partner_breakdown` contains exactly the group's members. A call carries at most one group: a GP calling several groups on the same schedule appears as sibling calls, one per group.

initiated_at.description: The date the call was initiated — notices go out and the funding clock starts. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch (UTC midnight of the initiation date).

livemode.description: Whether this object exists in live mode (`true`) or test mode (`false`).

partner_breakdown.description: Per-partner breakdown of the ask — one entry per partner the call reaches, ordered by partner identity, deduped across a partner's closings. Always inline, on lists and single reads; may be empty (an SPV's implicit call before any LP signs). The `called` amounts sum to `amount`. Partners awaiting their close are omitted — the fund has not called capital from them yet.

percentage_bps.description: Fraction of commitment called, in integer basis points (2500 = 25%; 10000 = 100%). The GP's canonical input — dollar amounts derive from it. Rounded half-even from venture's stored 12-decimal fraction; the money fields are computed from the full-precision value, so the rounding never moves money.

purpose.description: The GP-authored purpose of the call, as printed on the formal Capital Call Notice. Null when the GP left it blank (the notice then falls back to LPA boilerplate).

status.description: Due-date lifecycle, computed at read time from `due_at` alone: `completed` means the call is past its due date; it does not indicate whether the money arrived. `in_progress` means the due date has not fully passed — or no deadline exists yet (`due_at` is null). A call flips to `completed` 24 hours after `due_at` (midnight UTC after the due date), so it stays `in_progress` through the whole due day.

vehicle.description: The vehicle that issued this capital call.

has_more.description: Whether there are more items available after this page.

url.description: The URL for this list endpoint.

CapitalCallGroup.description: The LP group a capital call was issued to. Groups are a per-fund calling-policy feature; a group carries no public id yet, so it is identified by name within its vehicle.

name.description: The group's display name, unique within its vehicle.

is_default.description: Whether this is the vehicle's default group — the one new partners join automatically when the fund uses groups.

CapitalCallPartner.description: One partner's slice of a capital call's ask.

called.description: The amount this call asks of this partner — its slice of the call-level `amount`, from the same schedule computation. What was called, never what the partner paid.

PartnerRef.description: A reference to a partner by id. The `partner_` prefix encodes the type, so no `object` field is needed. The id is the same one `/v1/partners` and capital accounts use, stable across all of the organization's vehicles. Not expandable.

AssetClass.description: An asset class referenced on a vehicle's schedule of investments — a share class, convertible class, token type, or off-platform fund interest class.

id.description: Unique identifier for this asset class.

company.description: The portfolio investee this asset class belongs to. Omitted when the asset class has no linked corporation.

livemode.description: Whether this object exists in live mode (`true`) or test mode (`false`).

name.description: Display name of the asset class.

vehicle.description: The vehicle this asset class is scoped to.

has_more.description: Whether there are more items available after this page.

url.description: The URL for this list endpoint.

ValuationUpdate.description: An active accounting valuation mark on an asset class — either a fixed price-per-unit or a cost-basis multiplier as of an effective date. Convertible classes typically carry a `multiplier`; share classes and token types typically carry a `valuation`.

id.description: Unique identifier for this valuation update.

created.description: Time at which the valuation update was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.

asset_class.description: The asset class this valuation applies to on the vehicle's schedule of investments.

effective_date.description: Date the valuation takes effect. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch (UTC midnight of the effective calendar day).

livemode.description: Whether this object exists in live mode (`true`) or test mode (`false`).

multiplier.description: Cost-basis multiplier when the valuation is expressed as a fraction of original cost (e.g. `0.85` for 85%). Used for convertibles where unit count is unknown ahead of conversion. Omitted when the mark uses a fixed `valuation` instead.

valuation.description: Fixed price-per-unit mark. `amount` is in the currency's smallest unit — ISO cents for `USD`, or high-precision microcents for codes like `USD8` (preserved without downsampling). Omitted when the mark uses a `multiplier` instead.

vehicle.description: The vehicle this valuation update is scoped to.

has_more.description: Whether there are more items available after this page.

url.description: The URL for this list endpoint.

Asset.description:
A single portfolio position held by a vehicle, read from the schedule of investments on the vehicle's most recent financial statement.

Conventions: each monetary value is an `{amount, currency}` object carrying its own currency — the remaining cost basis (`remaining_cost_basis`) and the held mark (`unrealized_value`). These can differ — e.g. a USD wire into a foreign-domiciled fund that holds the position in INR. `date_purchased` is unix epoch seconds.

Source-of-truth policy: performance metrics live on the financial statement, not on this row. When the caller needs MOIC, TVPI, DPI, RVPI, IRR, NAV, fund-level paid-in / called / distributed, J-curve, or any gross-vs.-net-of-fees/carry cut, call `/v1/financial_statements` for the row's vehicle and read the canonical figure straight out of the body. Do NOT reconstruct performance metrics by combining or aggregating these values — the statement accounts for fees, carry, recyclables, FX, and cross-class reconciliation that the raw fields don't.

id.description: Unique identifier for this asset position. The underlying record id is encoded through a salted Sqid alphabet so the internal database identifier is never on the wire.

asset_class.description: The asset class this position belongs to on the vehicle's schedule of investments. Omitted when the position has no linked asset class.

date_purchased.description: Time at which the position was purchased. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch. Omitted for rows where no purchase date was recorded.

remaining_cost_basis.description: Remaining cost basis of the position — the amount paid to acquire it, less the basis attributed to any partial exits. The currency is almost always `USD` — funds typically wire in USD even when the underlying valuation is held in another currency. Omitted for rows where no cost was recorded.

unrealized_value.description: Most recent mark of the held position. May be stale relative to real-time market data. The currency may differ from `remaining_cost_basis` for foreign-domiciled funds (e.g. an India scheme that wires USD but values its held position in INR). Omitted when there's no valuation signal on the position.

investment_type.description: Instrument type of the position as recorded on the schedule of investments — e.g. `Preferred Stock`, `SAFE`, `Convertible Note`. Free-form text, not a closed enum. Omitted when no type was recorded.

remaining_shares.description: Number of shares (or units) still held for the position. May be fractional. Omitted for positions without a share count — e.g. SAFEs and convertible notes.

interest_rate_basis_points.description: Stated interest rate of the instrument, in basis points (an 8% note is `800`). Only present for interest-bearing instruments such as convertible notes.

accrued_interest.description: Interest accrued on the position and not yet realized, in the currency the interest is booked in (typically the currency of the invested principal). Omitted for non-interest-bearing positions.

last_valuation_action_date.description: Effective date of the most recent valuation applied to the position. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch. Only present for actively held positions on the schedule of investments; omitted for fully realized positions and when the position has no recorded valuation.

asset_events.description: Realization and conversion events recorded against the position, ordered oldest first. Each event aggregates the proceeds realized on a single date for one event type. Empty when the position has never been partially or fully realized.

company.description: The portfolio investee this position is in (corporation or platform fund). Omitted when the position has no linked investee.

livemode.description: Whether this object exists in live mode (`true`) or test mode (`false`).

vehicle.description: The vehicle this asset belongs to.

AssetEvent.description: A realization or conversion of an asset position on a single date. Multiple same-type dispositions on the same date are summed into one event. A conversion carries no cash proceeds — its cost basis rolls into the received position.

type.description: Kind of disposition. A `realization` is a cash exit; a `conversion` exchanges the position for another instrument and carries no cash proceeds.

date.description: Date the realization occurred. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch. Omitted when no date was recorded.

total_proceeds.description: Total cash proceeds realized on this date. Zero for conversions. Omitted when no proceeds were recorded.

num_units_liquidated.description: Number of units or shares disposed of in this event. Omitted when no unit count was recorded.

portfolio_interest.description: Interest collected as part of the realization — e.g. the accrued interest paid out when a note is repaid. Omitted when no interest was realized.

realized_gain_loss.description: Gain or loss recognized on this event, per the fund's ledger. Negative for a loss. Omitted when no gain or loss was recorded.

has_more.description: Whether there are more items available after this page.

url.description: The URL for this list endpoint.

Close.description: An investment closing on a vehicle. Each close represents a point in time when one or more partners formally committed capital to the vehicle. Closes are ordered by effective date. The `final` flag marks the last expected close for the vehicle — only one close per vehicle can be final.

id.description: Unique identifier for this close. The underlying record id is encoded through a salted Sqid alphabet so the internal database identifier is never on the wire.

created.description: Time at which the close was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.

commitment.description: Total commitment amount across all partners in this close.

contributed.description: Total contributed (paid-in) amount across all partners in this close.

effective_at.description: The date this close took effect. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch. Represents the date on which partners formally committed capital.

final.description: Whether this is the final close for the vehicle.

livemode.description: Whether this object exists in live mode (`true`) or test mode (`false`).

partner_count.description: Number of partners that committed capital in this close.

vehicle.description: The vehicle this close belongs to.

has_more.description: Whether there are more items available after this page.

url.description: The URL for this list endpoint.

FinancialStatement.description:
One financial-statement workbook (parsed JSON projection of the underlying xlsx) stored for a vehicle at a point in time, and the source of truth for fund performance metrics — MOIC, TVPI, DPI, RVPI, IRR, NAV, paid-in / called / distributed, J-curve, gross vs. net of fees/carry. Pull those off the `body` here rather than reconstructing them from `/v1/assets` fields. The `body` is opaque — a passthrough of the upstream JSON rendering of the workbook's sheets and cells (e.g. `Fund Summary`, `unaudited_SOI`, `SOC`, `Realizations`). Consumers should treat unknown keys gracefully; the upstream shape may grow new sheets and columns over time.

`/v1/assets` reads its rows from the vehicle's most recent statement.

id.description: Unique identifier for this financial statement. The underlying record id is encoded through a salted Sqid alphabet so the internal database identifier is never on the wire.

created.description: Time at which the financial-statement record was created in the upstream system. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch. Approximates the workbook's "as of" date for most statements but is the upstream record creation time, not a period-end date.

livemode.description: Whether this object exists in live mode (`true`) or test mode (`false`).

vehicle.description: The vehicle this financial statement belongs to.

as_of.description: The date this financial statement is "as of" — the period-end date the workbook was generated for. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch. Null when the upstream record lacks an as-of date.

period_type.description: Whether this statement is for the current open period (`interim`) or a finalized, closed quarter (`closed`). Use `closed` rows for historical EOQ snapshots and `interim` for the latest in-progress period.

document_id.description: Public ID of the document backing this statement's workbook file. Pass it to `getDocument` for the file's metadata and a short-lived download URL, or to `downloadDocument` to stream the file bytes. Null when no backing document exists. Statement documents are only addressable this way; they do not appear in `searchDocuments` results.

body.description: Parsed contents of the financial-statement workbook. Values are expressed in whole units of the fund's currency, not integer cents. The internal structure (sheet names, row shapes, cell values) is per-fund and may evolve; do not assume a fixed schema beyond "JSON object."

has_more.description: Whether there are more items available after this page.

url.description: The URL for this list endpoint.

type.description: Document category (snake_case). One of a fixed set: stock_purchase_agreement, convertible_equity_agreement, safe, note, warrant, agreement_for_future_tokens, token_purchase_agreement, token_warrant, token_warrant_purchase_agreement, token_warrant_exercise_notice, financial_statements. Search results only contain executed investment documents; financial_statements appears only when following a `document_id` from `listFinancialStatements` through `getDocument`.

PresignedUrl.description: A short-lived presigned URL for a file's bytes, plus its expiry. Not stable — do not cache or persist it.

url.description: Presigned URL for the file's bytes.

expires_at.description: When the URL expires, unix seconds. Absent until document-service reports it.

field.description: Field to filter on. `type` and `content_type` use `eq`; `created` (unix seconds) uses `gt`/`gte`/`lt`/`lte`; `q` (free text over the file name) uses `contains`.

DocumentSearchRequest.description: Search body. `vehicle` is required and scopes the search to one authorized vehicle. Optional predicate clauses filter within it.

vehicle.description: Public vehicle ID to scope the search to (required).

must.description: Predicates a document must all match (AND).

should.description: Predicates where at least one must match (OR).

must_not.description: Predicates a document must not match (NOT).

limit.description: Maximum number of documents to return (1-100, default 25).

starting_after.description: Cursor for forward pagination (a doc_ id).

BadRequest.description: The request was malformed or contained invalid parameters.

example.message: The 'limit' parameter must be between 1 and 100.
Access token is missing or invalid.

Forbidden.description: The authenticated user does not have permission to access this resource, or the vehicle's data is not available through the API. Vehicle-scoped financial-data endpoints return code `not_available` when a vehicle's data isn't served through the API yet — the API returns verified data or none, never partial data. One account can hold a mix of covered and uncovered vehicles; support for uncovered vehicles is on the roadmap and will be added in the coming months.

example.message: This vehicle's data is not currently available through the API. Support for this vehicle is in our roadmap and will be added in coming months.
The requested resource does not exist.
Too many requests. Please retry after the period specified in the Retry-After header.
An unexpected error occurred. Please try again or contact support with the request_id.

A close aggregates the total commitment amount, contributed amount, and partner count as of that date. The `final` flag marks the last expected close for the vehicle.
